name: Shopping and Consumers
blurb: Tiêu dùng, thương hiệu, giá cả

words.definitionEn: The preoccupation of society with the acquisition of consumer goods.
words.example: Modern consumerism often leads to overconsumption and environmental degradation.

words.definitionEn: The promotion of a particular product or company by means of advertising and distinctive design.
words.example: Effective branding can significantly increase customer loyalty and market share.

words.definitionEn: Relating to or denoting a product that is superior in quality and commands a higher price.
words.example: Many consumers are willing to pay a premium for organic food because of its health benefits.

words.definitionEn: A reduction from the usual price of something.
words.example: The store offered a 20% discount on all electronics during the holiday sale.

words.definitionEn: The sale of goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale.
words.example: The rise of online retail has transformed traditional shopping habits.

words.definitionEn: The sale of goods in large quantities to be retailed by others.
words.example: Wholesale prices are generally lower than retail prices due to bulk purchasing.

words.definitionEn: Commercial transactions conducted electronically on the Internet.
words.example: The growth of e-commerce has made shopping more convenient for consumers worldwide.

words.definitionEn: An unplanned purchase made on a sudden whim.
words.example: Impulse buys are often regretted later, especially when they exceed the consumer's budget.

words.definitionEn: The action of spending funds; an amount of money spent.
words.example: Household expenditure on luxury goods has increased steadily over the past decade.

words.definitionEn: An estimate of income and expenditure for a set period of time.
words.example: It is essential for consumers to set a monthly budget to avoid overspending.

words.definitionEn: The state of great comfort and extravagant living, or an expensive item that is not essential but desirable.
words.example: Luxury brands often rely on exclusivity to maintain their premium image.

words.meaningVi: nhu yếu phẩm, thứ cần thiết
words.definitionEn: A thing that is necessary for a particular purpose, especially a basic need.
words.example: Food and shelter are considered basic necessities for every individual.

words.definitionEn: An item bought or sold at a price lower than its usual value; a negotiation.
words.example: Finding a bargain in a crowded market requires patience and careful comparison.

words.definitionEn: A general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.
words.example: High inflation erodes consumers' purchasing power and reduces real income.

words.definitionEn: The desire of consumers for a particular good or service, backed by willingness to pay.
words.example: When demand for a product exceeds supply, prices tend to rise.

words.definitionEn: The amount of a product that is available for consumers to purchase.
words.example: Supply chain disruptions can lead to shortages and higher prices for consumers.

words.definitionEn: The exclusive control of a commodity or service in a particular market, giving the ability to set prices.
words.example: A monopoly in the market often results in higher prices for consumers with fewer choices.

words.definitionEn: The situation in which different businesses strive to attract customers and increase sales.
words.example: Intense competition among retailers often leads to lower prices and better quality for consumers.

words.definitionEn: The activity of producing advertisements to promote products or services.
words.example: Advertising plays a crucial role in shaping consumer preferences and brand perception.

words.definitionEn: The process of promoting, selling, and distributing a product or service.
words.example: Effective marketing strategies can significantly boost sales and customer engagement.

words.definitionEn: The tendency of customers to consistently purchase from the same brand over time.
words.example: Many companies offer loyalty programs to reward repeat customers and encourage brand loyalty.

words.definitionEn: A repayment of the full amount paid for a product or service, usually due to dissatisfaction or defect.
words.example: The store has a strict policy that any refund requires the original receipt.

words.definitionEn: A written guarantee promising to repair or replace a product if necessary within a specified period.
words.example: A longer warranty period often gives consumers more confidence in the quality of a product.

words.definitionEn: Made in exact imitation of something valuable or important with the intention to deceive.
words.example: Counterfeit goods not only harm the brand owner but also pose risks to consumer safety.

words.definitionEn: The ability to maintain or support a process continuously over time, especially in relation to environmental and social impact.
words.example: Consumers are increasingly prioritizing sustainability when making purchasing decisions.

words.definitionEn: A person who buys goods and services for personal use.
words.example: The modern consumer is increasingly concerned about the ethical sourcing of products.

words.definitionEn: To buy something.
words.example: Many consumers prefer to purchase goods online due to the convenience it offers.

words.definitionEn: The price of something, often shown on a label.
words.example: The price tag on luxury handbags can be exorbitant, reflecting the brand's exclusivity.

words.definitionEn: An item that is manufactured or refined for sale.
words.example: Companies invest heavily in research and development to improve their product quality.

words.definitionEn: A type of product manufactured by a particular company under a particular name.
words.example: Strong brand loyalty can insulate companies from price competition.

words.definitionEn: A person who visits shops to buy goods.
words.example: The rise of online shopping has transformed the behaviour of the average shopper.

words.definitionEn: A person who buys goods or services from a shop or business.
words.example: Excellent customer service is a key factor in retaining customers.

words.definitionEn: A person who uses the services of a professional organization.
words.example: Financial advisors must tailor their recommendations to each client's needs.

words.definitionEn: A person who regularly uses a particular shop, restaurant, or business.
words.example: The upscale boutique relies on a loyal patron base for its steady revenue.

words.definitionEn: A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold.
words.example: The price of commodities such as oil and wheat fluctuates based on global supply and demand.

words.definitionEn: Goods that are bought or sold in shops.
words.example: Retailers often display their merchandise in an attractive manner to boost sales.

words.definitionEn: A complete list of items such as property, goods in stock, or the contents of a building.
words.example: Efficient inventory management is crucial for avoiding stockouts and overstocking.

words.definitionEn: The goods available for sale in a shop.
words.example: The limited-edition sneakers were out of stock within hours of their release.

words.definitionEn: The sequence of processes involved in the production and distribution of a commodity.
words.example: Disruptions in the supply chain can lead to significant delays in product delivery.

words.definitionEn: The action of sharing something out among a number of recipients.
words.example: The company expanded its distribution network to reach rural areas more effectively.

words.definitionEn: The detailed organization and implementation of a complex operation, especially in business.
words.example: Advanced logistics systems enable same-day delivery for online shoppers.

words.definitionEn: The process of setting prices for products or services.
words.example: Competitive pricing strategies often involve careful analysis of the market.

words.definitionEn: The quality of being affordable; the extent to which something is within one's financial means.
words.example: The affordability of housing is a major concern for young families in urban areas.

words.definitionEn: The amount of money that households have available for spending and saving after income taxes have been accounted for.
words.example: An increase in disposable income often leads to higher consumer spending on non-essential items.

words.definitionEn: The financial ability to buy goods and services.
words.example: Currency depreciation reduces the purchasing power of consumers in the international market.

words.meaningVi: niềm tin của người tiêu dùng
words.definitionEn: An economic indicator measuring the degree of optimism that consumers feel about the overall state of the economy.
words.example: High consumer confidence typically encourages people to make major purchases like cars and homes.

words.definitionEn: A measure of how much the quantity demanded of a good responds to a change in its price.
words.example: Luxury goods often have low price elasticity because consumers are less sensitive to price changes.

words.definitionEn: A systematic approach to estimating the strengths and weaknesses of alternatives used to determine options that provide the best approach to achieve benefits.
words.example: A thorough cost-benefit analysis is essential before launching a new product line.

words.definitionEn: The loss of potential gain from other alternatives when one alternative is chosen.
words.example: The opportunity cost of spending money on a luxury vacation is the savings you could have invested.

words.definitionEn: A set of rules that a retailer follows regarding the acceptance of returned items.
words.example: A generous return policy can significantly boost customer trust and repeat purchases.
